turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here. It's 4:15 and I have a client call at 4:40, so I'd appreciate it if we got straight to it. You asked for this meeting, Hale.
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski.
Hale. Owen's zero was entered a week ago today, and I found out about it from him, on his phone, in the middle of class. What do you have to say about that?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent.
A machine's guess. The company that sells it says it shouldn't be the only basis for punishing a student. So what else do you have, Hale, or is that it?
That's very high. The software is quite reliable.
"Quite reliable." Okay. Fourteen detection tools were tested in one study and the finding was "neither accurate nor reliable." I'll ask once more: what else do you have besides a number?
So I had to give him a zero.
"Had to." Who decided that, Hale, and was Owen asked a single question before it went in the gradebook? Your own procedure says a parent gets a call before any mark is entered, and I didn't get one.
I hope you understand my position.

My position is that my son has a zero, nobody called me, and I'm writing down that you haven't answered either question. You've given me a score and a feeling, Hale. Is there a document, or am I going to the principal's office?
